  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) >

2 of 7. Another customer has chosen Pune, so the 'Today's offers' link includes the city. How should Pune appear in the link?
  A) Pune goes in exactly as it works today  B) Pune goes in tidied up (lower case, spaces replaced) so the same city never has two different links  C) Pune goes in only if it is one of the cities we serve; otherwise the customer gets the general page
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) >

3 of 7. The link can include an area (Koregaon Park) inside a city (Pune). A customer has given the area but no city. What should happen?
  A) Ignore the area too, and show the general offers page  B) Refuse the link, because an area means nothing without its city  C) Keep the area and assume our main city, Pune
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) >

4 of 7. The 'Track my order' link needs the order number, and a customer's message arrives without one. What should happen?
  A) Refuse, and show a clear 'we can't find that order' message as it does today  B) Send the customer to a general 'Track an order' page where they can type the number  C) Send the customer to their latest order automatically
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) >

We're asking what your website should do when a customer clicks 'Track my order' but their message didn't include an order number, so the site doesn't know which order they mean. You don't need to know any order number. This is a rule for what the site does in that situation. The first choice shows the customer a 'we can't find that order' message, which is what happens now. The second takes them to a general 'Track an order' page where they type in their number themselves. The third takes them straight to their most recent order without asking, which is quick but could show the wrong order if they have several.
  So, what should happen? (a letter, or your own words) >

  A) Refuse to create the link, and show an error  B) Quietly drop the city and show the general offers page  C) Guess the closest real city (Pune) and use that
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) >

7 of 7. A few older pages use links where the city is added without a label, so it can't be told apart from other details. What should we do about them?
  A) Leave them exactly as they are, and fix only the labelled ones  B) Fix these older pages in the same go, even though they currently work  C) List them for you to review first, and change none until you say so
  Your answer (a letter, or your own words) >

Some of your pages build their links by putting the city into the address with no label. Because of that, the system can't tell the city apart from any other detail in the link. The fix we're making is about labelled details. These older pages work today, but they could be affected by the change. The first choice leaves those older pages untouched and fixes only the labelled links, so nothing that works now is changed, but the older pages stay as they are. The second choice fixes the older pages at the same time, so everything is consistent, but pages that work today get changed. The third choice gives you a list of the older pages to look over first, and nothing is changed until you say so.
  So, what should happen? (a letter, or your own words) >
